title: Finite State Machine
description: Build a finite state machine library with guards, entry/exit actions, and hierarchical nested states.

steps.title: Define state and transition model
steps.description: Create data structures to represent states, events, and transitions. Define a `Transition` object with `fromState`, `event`, and `toState`. Create a `StateMachineConfig` that holds an initial state and an array of transitions. Build a simple config for a traffic light (green -> yellow -> red -> green) and print the transition table.
hints: Use plain objects: { from: 'green', event: 'timer', to: 'yellow' }
Group transitions by state for easy lookup later
Print the config as a formatted table showing each transition

verification.successMessage: State machine data model with transitions is correctly defined and printed!
verification.failureMessage: Define transitions for a traffic light (green->yellow->red->green) and print the transition table.

steps.title: Implement basic FSM class
steps.description: Build a `FiniteStateMachine` class with a constructor that takes a config. Implement a `getCurrentState()` method and a `transition(event)` method that looks up the matching transition, validates it, and updates the state. Print the current state before and after each transition. Handle invalid events gracefully.
hints: Build a transitions map: { fromState: { event: toState } } for O(1) lookups
If no transition is found for the current state + event, print 'Invalid transition' and return false
Return true on successful transition

verification.successMessage: FSM correctly transitions between states and validates events!
verification.failureMessage: Print the state before and after each transition. Show an error for invalid events.

steps.title: Add guards on transitions
steps.description: Extend transitions to support `guard` functions. A guard is a function that receives (currentState, event, context) and returns a boolean. If the guard returns false, the transition is blocked. Implement a door with states 'open', 'closed', 'locked' — only allow 'lock' from 'closed', and only allow 'unlock' if a key is provided. Print whether each transition was allowed.
hints: Add guard field to transition config: { from, event, to, guard: (ctx) => ... }
In transition(), check the guard before applying — if it returns false, print 'Transition blocked by guard'
Pass a context object through that guards can inspect

verification.successMessage: Guard functions correctly block or allow transitions based on conditions!
verification.failureMessage: Show that locking is only allowed from 'closed' and unlocking requires a key context.

steps.title: Implement entry and exit actions
steps.description: Add `onEnter` and `onExit` callback support to each state. Call `onExit(state)` on the current state before transitioning, and `onEnter(state)` on the new state after transitioning. Use a light switch FSM (on/off) that prints 'Turning on lights' on enter 'on' and 'Turning off lights' on exit 'on'. Print action logs.
hints: Store onEnter and onExit functions in the state config
Call onExit(currentState) BEFORE changing state, call onEnter(newState) AFTER
Log messages from inside the action callbacks so the user can see them

verification.successMessage: Entry and exit actions fire at the correct points during transitions!

steps.title: Add nested/hierarchical states
steps.description: Implement support for nested (hierarchical) states. A state can have child states with a `type: 'compound'` property. When in a child state, events not handled by the child should propagate to the parent. Use a media player example: 'stopped' -> 'playing' (with children 'playing.normal', 'playing.shuffle') -> 'paused'. Print the full state path (e.g. 'playing.shuffle').
hints: Track state as an array or dot-separated string to represent the hierarchy
When looking up a transition, check child states first, then fall back to the parent
Print the state as 'parent.child' when in a nested state

verification.successMessage: Hierarchical states with event propagation work correctly!
verification.failureMessage: Show the full dot-separated state path and demonstrate event propagation from child to parent.

steps.title: Implement event history
steps.description: Add a history feature that records every transition with a timestamp. Maintain a `history` array on the FSM instance where each entry is `{ fromState, toState, event, timestamp }`. Implement `getHistory()` returning the full history and `getLastTransitions(n)` returning the last n transitions. Print the full history after several transitions.
hints: Push a history entry object inside the transition() method after a successful transition
Use Date.now() or time.time() for the timestamp
getLastTransitions(n) can use array slicing from the end

verification.successMessage: Transition history is recorded with timestamps for every state change!
verification.failureMessage: Print the full transition history showing from, to, event, and timestamp for each entry.

steps.title: Build a visual state reporter
steps.description: Implement a `getStateGraph()` method that returns a printable string representation of the state machine structure. Show states and their transitions in a format like: 'green --[timer]--> yellow --[timer]--> red --[timer]--> green'. Include nested states indented under their parent. Print the graph to the console.
hints: Iterate over all transitions and format them as arrows
For nested states, indent children under the parent state name
Include the initial state marker: '-> initial_state'

verification.successMessage: State graph renders the full machine structure with transitions as arrows!
verification.failureMessage: Print a visual graph showing states connected by arrows labeled with event names.
